misconception_description: Student believes that colons (:) are used for variable assignment.

solutions.generated_code:
program MatriksIdentitas
kamus
  n, i, j : integer
  baris : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  for i <- 1 to n do
    baris : ""
    for j <- 1 to n do
      if i == j then
        baris : baris + "1 "
      else
        baris : baris + "0 "
      endif
    endfor
    output(baris)
  endfor
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced all assignment operators (=) with colons (:) throughout the code, believing this is the correct syntax for variable assignment in Python. They changed `matrix = []` to `matrix : []`, `row = [0] * n` to `row : [0] * n`, `i, j = tup` to `i, j : tup`, and `matrix[i][j] = 1` to `matrix[i][j] : 1`. The student is confident this is the proper way to assign values to variables and expects the code to work correctly. This will result in SyntaxError when the code is executed.
